A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ZILOT research work. Their complete main texts and appendices A–E are readable, and text and visual inspection support comparison of the methods, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulation experiments across 30 tasks in five environments, including baseline comparisons, ablations and qualitative trajectory analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds Walker evaluation results in Appendix A.4 and Table 3.

M1.justification: The learned dynamics, value functions, OT objective, Sinkhorn computation and MPC procedure remain unchanged. Appendix C.2 expands the documentation of existing GC-TD-MPC2 training; it does not report a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix A.4 adds Walker with eight locomotion tasks, reusing HalfCheetah's goal space, task definitions and data-collection approach. This extends coverage to related environment dynamics while retaining all original benchmarks.

E2.justification: The original comparisons retain ERFB, RERFB, Pi+Cls and MPC+Cls. The added Walker evaluation reuses Pi+Cls and MPC+Cls; it introduces no new comparator or replacement in an existing experiment.

E3.justification: Appendix C.3 replaces the runtime measurement hardware from a reported 2080 Ti GPU to an RTX 4090. The original training budgets, goal sampling, evaluation metrics and threshold searches remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations, horizon sweep, single-goal checks, dataset-coverage analysis, threshold searches and FB training curves are retained. Walker adds benchmark coverage and scores without a distinct ablation, perturbation test or error-analysis protocol.

E5.justification: Tables 1–2 retain means over 20 trials, standard deviations across five seeds and Welch t-tests at p = 0.05. Existing uncertainty displays are unchanged, and the Walker entries introduce no newly specified statistical procedure or increased run count.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and existing graphical results are unchanged. New Table 3 reports Walker results, including aggregate Wmin of 1.174 ± 0.061 for ZILOT versus 1.436 ± 0.049 for MPC+Cls. Appendix C.3 replaces ZILOT's 0.5–3 Hz with 2–4 Hz and MPC+Cls's 12–35 Hz with 25–72 Hz on different hardware, so these are not comparable-setting speedups.

T1.justification: Appendix C.2 adds explicit mathematical definitions of the combined training loss, SAC-style policy objective and auxiliary value-regression loss, including clipped TD targets (Equations 21–23). Proposition 3.1, its proof and the OT derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the same central contribution: reducing myopia in zero-shot offline imitation through OT occupancy matching with learned dynamics and goal-conditioned values.

C2.justification: Section 2.1 adds a computational qualification to the zero-shot setting: modest inference overhead and largely avoiding network updates. Appendix A.4 interprets Walker's results as resembling HalfCheetah's. Existing world-model and finite-horizon limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 newly documents loss terms, stop-gradient use, rewards, TD targets and auxiliary value-function training. Appendix A.4 explains Walker's reuse of existing task and collection definitions, while C.3 updates runtime hardware. Existing hyperparameters and code access are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Haarnoja et al. (2018) for SAC-style training and Tassa et al. (2018) for the Walker environment. The substantive related-work discussion and positioning against prior imitation methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes comprise focused expansions in Sections 2.1 and C.2, the new A.4 subsection, and small heading, affiliation and publication-text edits. Most prose and the overall section structure are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 3, combining new Walker scores with repeated HalfCheetah results. Tables 1–2 move earlier within Appendix A, and several existing figures and tables are repositioned. All existing embedded graphics are reused.

improvement.justification: The explicit training objectives and TD targets improve implementation transparency, while the Walker evaluation modestly broadens empirical support without altering existing evidence. These gains are limited: new Equation 22 contains ambiguous rollout notation, and the changed GPU prevents interpreting the higher runtime rates as an algorithmic improvement.
